title: Translating Words into Expressions
_notes: Source of truth for the 0.5 practice set. Kind "words": the learner types an expression for a sentence; any equal form is right (anyForm). Each answer is pinned by a test, "means" computed from the sentence at a real value of the variable; the answer must give that value and every wrong option a different one. Variables: only x, y, z, a, b, c can be checked. "multi" uses check equals:<expr>; "match" uses check "operation" (key words in OPERATION_WORDS). Chips: VAR blue, WORDS yellow, ORDER purple, GROUP green, TEST ink. See docs/exercises.md.

exercises.prompt: Match each phrase with the operation it means.
exercises.read: Match each phrase with the operation it means.
exercises.say_answer: Every phrase now has its operation. Increased by adds, less than and difference subtract, twice multiplies, and per divides.

pairs.say: Increased by means more, so it is addition.
The difference of two numbers comes from subtracting them.
Twice means two times, so it is multiplication.

pairs.why: Per means for each, which is dividing.
pairs.say: Per means for each, which is division.
Less than means take away, so it is subtraction.

exercises.prompt: Write an expression for “a number increased by seven”. Use x for the number.
exercises.read: Write an expression for: a number increased by seven. Use x for the number.
say: Let x be the number.
Increased by means add, so x plus seven.

wrong.why: Increased by means add, not multiply.
Increased means more, so you add. Subtracting makes it smaller.
Increased by means add, and the number comes first.

exercises.prompt: Write an expression for “the product of three and a number”. Use x for the number.
exercises.read: Write an expression for: the product of three and a number. Use x for the number.
lines: The product of three and ⟨a number⟩
say: Let x be the number.
Product means multiply, and three times x is written three x.

wrong.why: Product means multiply, not add.
Product means multiply, not subtract.
Product means multiply, not divide.

exercises.prompt: Write an expression for “five less than a number”. Use x for the number.
exercises.read: Write an expression for: five less than a number. Use x for the number.
say: Call the number x.
Less than reverses the order: start from x and take away five, so x minus five.

wrong.why: The words come in the opposite order from the symbols: start from x.
wrong.say: write the numbers in the order you hear them

wrong.why: Less than means subtract, not multiply.
Less than means take away, not add.

exercises.prompt: Select all that mean “seven less than a number x”.
exercises.read: Which of these mean seven less than a number x? Choose all that apply.
exercises.say_answer: Two of them mean seven less than x: x minus seven, and negative seven plus x. Less than starts from the number and takes seven away.

options.why: Start from x and take away seven.
options.say: x minus seven. Start from x and take away seven. Right.

options.why: Same value as x − 7, written in a different order.
options.say: Negative seven plus x. Adding in a different order gives the same value as x minus seven.

options.why: This starts from 7, not from x.
options.say: Seven minus x starts from seven, so it is the opposite order. Not a match.
x plus seven adds. Less than means subtract.
Seven x multiplies. Not a match.

exercises.prompt: Write an expression for “the quotient of a number and six”. Use x for the number.
exercises.read: Write an expression for: the quotient of a number and six. Use x for the number.
lines: The quotient of ⟨a number⟩ and six
say: Let x be the number.
Quotient means divide, with x on top and six on the bottom.

wrong.why: The quotient of a and b is a divided by b: the first number goes on top.
Quotient means divide, not subtract.
Quotient means divide, not multiply.

exercises.prompt: Write an expression for “twice the sum of a number and three”. Use x for the number.
exercises.read: Write an expression for: twice the sum of a number and three. Use x for the number.
exercises.a_read: two times the quantity x plus three
lines: Twice ⟨the sum of a number and three⟩
say: With x as the number, the sum of a number and three is a group: x plus three, in parentheses.
Twice means times two, so two times the whole group.

wrong.why: Twice applies to the whole sum, so the sum needs parentheses.
You still have to double the sum.
Sum means add, not subtract.
wrong.read: two times the quantity x minus three

exercises.prompt: Write an expression for “three more than twice a number”. Use x for the number.
exercises.read: Write an expression for: three more than twice a number. Use x for the number.
say: With x as the number, twice a number is two x.
Three more than two x means start from two x and add three.

wrong.why: The three is added after the doubling; only the number is doubled.
Twice a number is just 2x; the three is added after, with no parentheses.
wrong.read: two times the quantity x plus three

wrong.why: More than means add, not subtract.

exercises.prompt: Select all that mean “twice the sum of x and three”.
exercises.read: Which of these mean twice the sum of x and three? Choose all that apply.
exercises.say_answer: Two of them are right: two times the quantity x plus three, and two x plus six. The second is the first with the two distributed.

options.say: Two times the quantity x plus three. Add first, then double. Right.
Two x plus six is two times the quantity x plus three, with the two distributed. Right.

options.why: Only the x is doubled here.
options.say: Two x plus three doubles only the x. Not a match.

options.why: This adds six to x without doubling it.
options.say: x plus six does not double the x. Not a match.

options.why: This adds two instead of multiplying.
options.say: Two plus the quantity x plus three adds two. Twice means multiply.

exercises.prompt: Tickets cost 12 dollars each and popcorn costs 6. A 3 dollar coupon is taken off. Write an expression for the cost of x tickets and one popcorn.
exercises.read: Tickets cost twelve dollars each and popcorn costs six. A three dollar coupon is taken off. Write an expression for the cost of x tickets and one popcorn.
lines: ⟨x tickets at 12 each⟩, popcorn 6, coupon 3 off
say: Tickets cost twelve each, so x tickets cost twelve x.
The popcorn adds six.
The coupon takes off three.
Now combine the constants: six minus three is three, so twelve x plus three.

wrong.why: A coupon takes money off: subtract it, don't add it.
Only the tickets get the 12.
wrong.say: multiply the popcorn by twelve too
wrong.read: twelve times the quantity x plus six, minus three

wrong.why: You still have to take off the coupon.

exercises.prompt: Write an expression for “seven less than the product of three and a number”. Use x for the number.
exercises.read: Write an expression for: seven less than the product of three and a number. Use x for the number.
lines: Seven less than ⟨the product of three and a number⟩
say: With x as the number, the product of three and a number is three x.
Seven less than three x means start from three x and take away seven.

wrong.why: Less than starts from the other quantity: three x comes first.
wrong.say: write the numbers in the order you hear them

wrong.why: The seven comes off the product, not off the number first.
wrong.read: three times the quantity x minus seven

wrong.why: Less than means subtract, not add.

exercises.prompt: Write an expression for “four times the difference of a number and nine”. Use x for the number.
exercises.read: Write an expression for: four times the difference of a number and nine. Use x for the number.
exercises.a_read: four times the quantity x minus nine
lines: Four times ⟨the difference of a number and nine⟩
say: With x as the number, the difference of a number and nine is a group: x minus nine, in parentheses.
Four times means multiply the whole group by four.

wrong.why: The four multiplies the whole difference, so it needs parentheses.
Difference of a number and nine starts with the number: x − 9.
wrong.read: four times the quantity nine minus x

wrong.why: Times means multiply, not divide.
